newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed, PGMs stay firm.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed, PGMs stay firm.

text.p: Platinum group metals (PGMs) took the spotlight on Tuesdsay afternoon as rates for borrowing the metal against trading commitments soared and even modest buying sent prices higher.

Dealers said gold and silver stayed in the shadows as the PGMs rebounded after losing ground last week on news that Russia would begin its delayed 1997 export campaign at the end of this month or the beginning of June.
Gold was fixed at $343.65 up just 10 cents from the the morning fixing and compared to $342.55 on Friday afternoon.
The June contract on New York's Comex market was at $344.40 up $1.30 at the afternoon fixing.
Silver was also little changed from morning levels at $4.74/$4.76 and unchanged from Friday's London close which was elevated by a late fund-led short covering rally, dealers said.
Last week's easier tone in the PGMs turned round abruptly this morning when borrowing in volume of palladium for dates six months and 12 months out shook the market.

Dealers noted that the already tight palladium market clenched further with one-month lease rates now at 40 percent versus 25 percent last week and as little as two or three percent in a more normally balanced market.
Even the one-year rate for palladium was at 17 percent.
"People seem to be getting wise to it and buying the metal to lend it out," a dealer said, but he added that hedging was much safer given the recent volatility in the palladium price.
"In money terms its not that much (to borrow). If you bought palladium you run the risk of it being $10 or $15 lower the next day," he added.

Supply to the PGM market has been disrupted all this year after Russia, the main exporter or palladium and second largest supplier of platinum has failed to ship metal since last December, including to Japan its main customer.
Some dealers said it would be at least four weeks before Russia started shipping to Japan even if talks began on schedule June. Others thought shipments would begin more quickly
Platinum rose largely on the back of the palladium market and failed to break $400 when it was its rise.
"It didn't really seriously test $400. They (sellers) were coming in before it got there," one dealer said.
Dealers also noted that tomorrow's over the counter (OTC) expiry could also be limiting extremes of price moves today.
